record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Ex ante core with strategic externalities
record.original_question: How should the ex ante core be defined for cooperative games with incomplete information when strategic externalities are present, so that the definition properly accounts for the fact that the actions of players outside a coalition can affect that coalition's members' payoffs?

evidence.quote: One important question, still open, is what would be appropriate definitions of the ex ante core in contexts with strategic externalities.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cooperative game with incomplete information specified as follows. There is a finite set of players $N = \{1,\dots,n\}$ and, for each player $i\in N$, a finite set $T_i$ of types, with $T=\prod_{i\in N}T_i$. A common prior $p\in\Delta(T)$ describes the joint distribution of types. Each player $i$ has a set of feasible actions (or strategies) $A_i$, and payoffs are given by functions $u_i:A\times T\to\mathbb{R}$, where $A=\prod_{j\in N}A_j$. A coalition $S\subseteq N$ chooses a (possibly type-contingent) joint plan $\sigma_S:T_S\to A_S$, while players outside $S$ choose plans $\sigma_{N\setminus S}:T_{N\setminus S}\to A_{N\setminus S}$. Because $u_i$ depends on the full action profile, the realized payoff to members of $S$ depends on the behavior of $N\setminus S$; this is the situation of "strategic externalities."

An allocation (or outcome) is a mapping $x:T\to\mathbb{R}^n$ (or more generally a joint plan together with type-contingent transfers) that is feasible for the grand coalition $N$. Player $i$'s ex ante payoff from $x$ is $U_i(x)=\sum_{t\in T}p(t)\,u_i(\sigma(t),t)+\mathbb{E}[x_i]$ as appropriate.

Problem: Provide a definition of the ex ante core for such games in the presence of strategic externalities. Concretely, specify
(a) what it means for a coalition $S$ to "block" an ex ante allocation $x$, taking into account that the deviating coalition $S$ must form expectations or assumptions about the action choices of the complement $N\setminus S$ (e.g., $\alpha$-effective, $\beta$-effective, Nash-consistent, or rational-expectation responses), and how these assumptions interact with type-contingent information and incentive-compatibility constraints; and
(b) the resulting set of unblocked ex ante allocations (the ex ante core), in such a way that the definition reduces to the standard ex ante core when payoffs are coalitionally separable (no strategic externalities) and yields a meaningful, internally consistent solution concept otherwise.

Justify that the proposed definition properly accounts for the influence of outsiders' actions on coalition members' payoffs.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of what constitute appropriate definitions of the ex ante core in cooperative games with incomplete information and strategic externalities is described as an open problem. Related work on partition-form games, alpha/beta cores under uncertainty, and incentive-compatible ex ante cores exists, but no single canonical definition has been established. Recent papers (e.g., interim core corrections on arXiv 1903.09867, work on the ex ante core for normal form games with uncertainty) propose partial answers in restricted settings but do not resolve the general problem.

status_evidence.title: Cooperative Analysis of Incomplete Information (Liu, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ex ante, interim and ex post core notions and notes difficulties arising from strategic externalities in coalitional analysis.
status_evidence.claim: The literature continues to discuss multiple competing core definitions without a settled treatment of strategic externalities.

status_evidence.title: The ex ante α-core for normal form games with uncertainty
status_evidence.snippet: Defines an ex ante alpha-core for normal form games with uncertainty.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist defining alpha-type ex ante cores in special frameworks, but a general definition with strategic externalities remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: An interim core for normal form games and exchange economies with incomplete information: a correction
status_evidence.snippet: Corrects interim core definitions, indicating ongoing refinement of core concepts under incomplete information.
status_evidence.claim: Core definitions under incomplete information are still actively being refined.
